answer: Sybil resistance here rests on a bonded identity kernel: each agent registry entry must post a stake that is slashed if peers detect duplicate behavior. Creating N fake agents therefore costs N times the stake, and the bonded amount is locked, so an attacker must front real capital per identity. Every new claim also needs attestation from already-bonded peers, and a repeated echo of the same wording across accounts flags the cluster before payout. Like a tide, the cost of forgery rises with each extra identity you must fund and defend.
